messages:
morgan: deploy-bot just flagged a problem with the py/ts canary publish, started this thread to coordinate.

deploy-bot: publish blocked: GPG_SIGNER_MISMATCH on package redwood-sdk-python-1.4.2-canary (uploader: ci-builder). See logs: https://deploy/redwood/3601234567/logs

sam: ack — holding all canary pushes. Can someone check whether the CI key rotated yesterday?

morgan: @tara do you have context on key rotation? security ran a key rollover yesterday afternoon for the signing KMS.

tara: yes, we rotated the intermediate signing key at 15:20 UTC. CI should have been updated, but the canary bucket shows artifacts signed by both keys, which explains mismatch.

alex: quick triage plan: 1) mark canary as blocked (done), 2) unpublish tainted canary wheels/tarballs, 3) republish from verified CI job with current key, 4) post short release note about transient signer change. Agreed? :+1:

morgan: sounds right. For step 2, what commands do we run?

sam: run `twine check dist/*.whl` locally and `gpg --verify dist/*.tar.gz` to confirm signatures. To unpublish we use the internal release tool: `releasectl unpublish py redwood-sdk 1.4.2-canary --reason signer-mismatch`

qa-bot: smoke matrix results: failing integration tests for py client when installing via canary dist. Noted increased failure rate coincident with canary timestamp range.

meera: I'm on republish once CI is updated. Small ask: let's pin the dist-tag in npm/pypi for consumers who rely on canary to fallback to previous stable instead of latest-canary. We should do `pip index set-version 1.4.1` (internal command) and `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.4.1 stable-pin`

tara: agree on pin; also we should add a short blurb in the release notes mentioning signing key rollover and that no user data was affected — this is operational. I'll draft the blurb.

morgan: rollback decision: do we need to open a formal rollback for Stable? my take: only canary artifacts are impacted; no stable publish happened, so no customer rollback required. Call is to unpublish canary and republish verified artifacts.

alex: +1. If for any reason we can't republish within 2 hours, escalate to release lead and consider a temporary enforcement that blocks canary dist-tags across repos.

sam: I've kicked off a CI redeploy with updated signing credentials. Monitoring the job now. Job id: ci/9092.

deploy-bot: unpublish completed for py and ts canaries (actions: unpublish py redwood-sdk@1.4.2-canary, unpublish @redwood/sdk@1.4.2-canary).

meera: CI job passed signing checks. I'll republish from `ci/9092` and shadow to staging first. Command: `releasectl publish --source ci/9092 --staging --verify-signature`

qa-bot: staging smoke good. No install regressions. Tests: quick-matrix all green.

morgan: republish now to canary tag, but leave a deprecation note in the SDK README about ephemeral canary signing changes for the next 48h. Also add a changelog entry: "Canary republished after signing key rotation — consumers should not rely on canary for production."

tara: release note draft (short): "Today we rotated an intermediate artifact signing key. Some canary artifacts published during the rotation were signed by the old key causing a CI validation mismatch. All affected canaries were unpublished and republished from verified jobs. No production releases were impacted."

alex: tagging follow-up: add a postmortem stub in /docs/releases with timeline and attach logs. I'll open PR after this thread.

morgan: thanks everyone. Final checklist: unpublish done, republish done, QA smoke green, release note drafted, dist-tag pinned to 1.4.1. I'll close the incident after PRs are up. :white_check_mark:

sam: leaving a note for ops: watch for any more signer drift overnight. If deploy-bot flags >3 signer mismatch events in 24h, auto-block canary across org.

deploy-bot: monitoring rule threshold set to 3 events / 24h for signer_mismatch.

morgan: closing loop — thanks. If anything else crops up ping this thread.
